rows.evidence: The only production writer of `snapshots` is UPSERT_SNAPSHOT_SQL (src/core/record-store/sqlite-record-store.ts:102), used in the commit loop at sqlite-record-store.ts:466 after planPreparedCommit re-decodes the body (record-codec.ts:560) and runs the registered schema (record-codec.ts:638; cursor-bound records again at :730/:737); the column is TEXT NOT NULL (migrations.ts:19). So the text currentRevisionOf reads at :330 was always produced by the same decodeGuardedRevision (guarded-revision.ts:12-22) and can only fail it after an out-of-band UPDATE or with an old-format body (decision 79-1). Checked for other writers/paths: sqlite-lookup-indexes.ts and sqlite-text-scan.ts only read json; sqlite-body-store.ts writes a separate `artifacts` table; app/UI/tools/CLI all go through this one backend; a concurrent same-ref commit is caught as revision_conflict at :416-417, never here. The before-T coverage was the direct `UPDATE snapshots` test (before/tests/record-store/R3a-transaction-boundaries.test.ts:123, T2-010).
rows.proposal_note: Keep, untested. This is the corrupt-not-conflict diagnostic described at sqlite-record-store.ts:317-323, not an old-format reader; AGENTS rule 4 and slice-1-book-part1.md:44 (never write a broken record into a DB to reach a corruption branch) forbid restoring the tampering test, and deleting the branch would report a damaged guard row as a revision conflict.

rows.evidence: guardConflicts only propagates currentRevisionOf's invalid at sqlite-record-store.ts:344-345, i.e. the damaged guard row of A3-033 (row exists, text body fails decodeGuardedRevision, guarded-revision.ts:19-22) or a guard whose refKey is itself non-canonical/unregistered. The latter has no production source: guard builders use canonicalRefKey/canonicalOf of real refs (e.g. query-execution.ts:1323, mailbox-service.ts:3501, task-service.ts:244-245), and externally supplied pins never become guards directly - exactPinSet (decision-service.ts:540-559) and validateExpected (query-execution.ts:694-742) require them to equal the card's/operation's own pins. A missing row is decoded as null, not invalid (sqlite-record-store.ts:326, guarded-revision.ts:18). Only an outside UPDATE or an old-format row reaches :345; before-T coverage was the same tampering test (before/tests/record-store/R3a-transaction-boundaries.test.ts:123, T2-010).
rows.proposal_note: Keep, untested. No platform writer produces a damaged or non-canonical guard row today; the theoretical non-canonical guard key would be an internal programming error, and keeping the propagation is safer than degrading it to a conflict. No test should tamper (AGENTS rule 4).

rows.evidence: The arm at sqlite-record-store.ts:381 is the stored-body decode in readManyInside (:375-381). Every body written by commit had already passed decodeRecordBody and applyRecordSchema (record-codec.ts:560, :638, and commit re-serializes that parsed body at sqlite-record-store.ts:466), so readMany/readManyInside is deterministic for a same-build DB. Callers only choose keys: readMany (:818), ordered lookup (:682), text search (:797). A caller-supplied non-canonical key is rejected earlier as `invalid` at :358, an unregistered type as `unsupported` at :360-363, and a vanished row becomes `missing` (:370-373) - none of those is this arm. Only a hand-edited/old-format body (decision 79-1) reaches it; before-T coverage was the direct UPDATE test (before/tests/record-store/lookup.test.ts:194-198, T2-017).
rows.proposal_note: Keep, untested. This is the read-boundary integrity check that keeps a damaged row from being returned as another aggregate's record; it is not version-dispatch/old-format code, and the tampering test may not be restored (AGENTS rule 4, slice-1-book-part1.md:44).

rows.evidence: commitInsideTransaction rejects a guard decode failure at sqlite-record-store.ts:412-414; guardConflicts (:344-345) returns invalid only from currentRevisionOf (:324-334), i.e. a stored guard row whose text body was rewritten outside the platform or an old-format body. The normal CAS case is the next branch: the same observed revision is fed to guardIsSatisfied and a mismatch becomes revision_conflict at :416-417. No other producer of snapshot rows exists (single writer UPSERT_SNAPSHOT_SQL, :102/:466, after record-codec.ts:560/:638), and caller pins are checked against the operation's own refs before they become guards (decision-service.ts:540-559, query-execution.ts:694-742). Before-T coverage was the tampering test before/tests/record-store/R3a-transaction-boundaries.test.ts:123 (T2-010).
rows.proposal_note: Keep, untested. Deleting the propagation would make a corrupt guard row indistinguishable from a real version conflict; rule 4 forbids a test that tampers with the database, so keep it uncovered.

rows.evidence: In lookupInside the candidates come from the registered index: the WHERE clause is `aggregateTypeTerm(index.aggregateType)` on ref_key (sqlite-record-store.ts:562, :575), and every stored ref_key/body was validated at commit (record-codec.ts:560/:638; sqlite-record-store.ts:466), so readManyInside (:582) can only fail at :583 on a row whose key or body no longer decodes (hand-edited or old-format, decision 79-1). The other outcomes are handled separately: SQL/index errors at :577-578, a vanished row as `missing` at :584-585, and the read runs in one read transaction (:602) so a concurrent writer cannot change the row between the candidate SELECT and the read (and would only produce a newer valid body). Before-T coverage was before/tests/record-store/lookup.test.ts:194-198 (direct UPDATE, T2-017).
rows.proposal_note: Keep, untested. It is the lookup integrity propagation (a damaged candidate must read as corrupt, not as another record); no platform writer produces the shape, and the tampering test cannot be restored under AGENTS rule 4.
